summary: Static verification for Minecraft Fabric mod 'Native Client' (Java project, no web app). Ran the exact Gradle command requested: compileJava, compileUi26Java, compileUimcJava, compileTestJava with JDK 25 at /root/jdk/jdk-25.0.4.1+1 - all four source sets compiled successfully (exit 0). Did NOT run game, build, jar, test or release per user instruction. Reviewed the five changed areas (leave-world fix, custom items pipeline, Armor HUD, Inventory HUD grid, Setting.Choice.initial).

code_review_findings.Leave-world (UiRuntime.leaveWorld / McBr: Correct. UiRuntime.leaveWorld() guards re-entry with the `leaving` flag, captures `mc.gameThread()` and posts `mc.exitWorld()` via Executor.execute() from a daemon 'Native leave world' helper thread -- so exitWorld (which calls setScreen(PauseScreen(true)) and simulates the vanilla Disconnect button press, nesting its own renderFrame/setScreenAndShow) runs on the next game tick instead of inside our active frame hook, which fixes the blank-blurred stuck screen with only the watermark. `leaving` is reset in finally. MojangMc.gameThread() returns Minecraft.getInstance() (Minecraft extends ReentrantBlockableEventLoop which implements Executor). IntermediaryMc.gameThread() casts class_310 to Executor (MinecraftClient extends ThreadExecutor on every supported version). Both exitWorld impls set UiRuntime.pauseBypass=true before showing the vanilla PauseScreen so replaceScreen doesn't re-replace it with our host, press the matching Disconnect / Save-and-Quit button via onPress()/method_25306 reflection, and restore pauseBypass in finally. Translations fetched from tr() with the exact vanilla keys. Thread-safety: UiRuntime.leaving is volatile; `mc` is written only in install() before any frame hook can run; capture-into-local for `game` executor is safe.
code_review_findings.Custom items (Game.Slot + stack + Vanill: Correct. Game.Slot now carries `model` (item_model id) and `cmd` (first CustomModelData float, NaN when none); set()/clear() reset both; custom() nulls model when it equals the plain item id so the fast path (plain item icon) is used. MojangMc.stack reads DataComponents.ITEM_MODEL and CUSTOM_MODEL_DATA.getFloat(0) and wraps the whole thing in try/catch so broken packs just show the plain icon. IntermediaryMc.customLook reads class_9334 field_54199/field_49637 reflectively via method_58694(ComponentType) (1.20.5+), then CustomModelData.comp_3354 (1.21.4+ List<Float>) or comp_2382 (1.20.5-1.21.3 int), falling back to NBT method_7969 + method_10545/method_10550('CustomModelData') on 1.16-1.20.4. Any ReflectiveOperationException bubbles up into stack()'s catch -> plain icon. Vanilla.item(Slot) short-circuits when model==null && cmd NaN (plain path), otherwise fromModel(model|id, cmd) with assets/<ns>/items/<id>.json (1.21.4+ definitions) -> pick() with range_dispatch/condition/select/composite/special/model; also override() for pre-1.21.4 overrides. All JsonElement.getAsFloat / getAsInt / getAsString calls are inside the outer try/catch in item(Slot) so a malformed pack entry only costs the custom icon, not the UI. Namespaced ids correctly use assets/<ns>/ and prepend 'minecraft:' only when no colon present.
code_review_findings.Armor HUD (StatusModules.Armor): Correct. style.initial(STYLE_TEXT) sets both value and def (via Choice.initial), so reset-to-default targets Text instead of Icons. text default is 1 (Percent). List layout (layout.value==0): rowH=ic+3s; measure pass computes max textWidth once, w=ic+(tw>0?gap+tw:0). On the right half (fx>0.5) ix = x+pad+w-ic (icons flush right) and the number sits at ix-gap-t0 (left of the icon); otherwise ix=x+pad and text at ix+ic+gap. Measure (ui==null) and draw sizes match: done(w+2*pad, n*rowH-3s+2*pad). For non-damageable items label() returns String.valueOf(carried(g, sl)) which, when `total` is on and NEED_INVENTORY has been requested, sums every matching stack across the 36 inventory slots plus the off-hand, min 1 - that gives the '177 total arrows' behaviour. same() correctly uses id + model (null-safe) + cmd (NaN-safe) so stacks of identical custom items are summed and base-id stacks aren't mixed with custom-model variants. Row layout preserved and unchanged. Empty slots (shown when `empty` setting on) use the soft rounded tile (ic*0.8 inner) in drawSlot - no NPE because label() returns '' for sl.empty() and item() isn't called.
code_review_findings.Inventory HUD (StatusModules.InventoryGr: Correct. New Choice setting 'layout' with Horizontal/Vertical, default 0. Horizontal uses 9 cols x (3 + optional hotbar) rows (step=21s, cell=20s, extra 4s sep between inventory and hotbar). Vertical swaps axes: along stays 9 cells, across stays rows. w/h math: w=(vertical?across:along)+2*pad, h=(vertical?along:across)+2*pad - symmetric and the measure (ui==null) path uses the same formula. Dark rounded cells c.round(sx,sy,cell,cell,3s,0x66000000) with a thin top sheen; selected hotbar slot gets a bright outline. Counts in Fonts.BOLD at 10.5s, bottom-right (sx+cell-tw-0.5s, sy+cell-flh+1.5s). pad() override returns 4s for CARD/BRACKETS and 0 otherwise. drop(labels, color) correctly removes the inherited labels/color pickers from this module's settings.
code_review_findings.Setting.Choice.initial(int): Correct. Choice.initial(v) sets both value and def and returns `this`, so Armor's `style.initial(STYLE_TEXT)` makes STYLE_TEXT the reset target as well as the starting value. load()/save() round-trip through the label (options[value]), so a saved file carrying the old default still loads to the matching index without clobbering the new one.

critical_code_review_comments: StatusModules.java is now 600 lines (up from 574). Still OK but trending toward the 700-line split guideline; splitting Armor and InventoryGrid into their own files would help maintainability.

Armor.label() ignores the text.value 'Off' choice for non-damageable items (always shows the carried count). This matches the user requirement ('non-damageable items show the total carried count') but might surprise users who turn text off expecting nothing - consider documenting or honouring 'Off' there too.

Vanilla.pick() calls JsonElement.getAsFloat / getAsInt without primitive checks; this is safely contained by the outer try/catch in item(Slot) but a non-numeric 'threshold'/'scale'/'index' in a user pack silently falls back to the plain icon rather than logging a one-time diagnostic. Minor, cosmetic.

IntermediaryMc.exitWorld() iterates widgets looking for either 'Save and Quit to Title' or 'Disconnect' by exact translated string compare; if the player uses a resource pack that overrides those keys to text containing padding (e.g. trailing space) the match will miss and the vanilla pause screen will stay open with pauseBypass momentarily true (then flipped back in finally). Not a bug per se - the fallback behaviour is documented in the code comments.
